nodes.label: Go html/template Partial Composition Pattern
nodes.rationale: No template engine inheritance exists in Go html/template, so page templates achieve layout reuse by {{template "head"}} / "navbar" / "sidebar" / "footer" composition. Every admin page repeats the same four-call prologue, meaning the layout contract is a naming convention over the global template set rather than a structural parent relationship: renaming a partial silently breaks every page.

nodes.label: AdminLTE 3 Admin Theme Contract
nodes.rationale: The admin shell depends on AdminLTE 3 class names (content-wrapper, content-header, sidebar-mini, main-sidebar, nav-sidebar, has-treeview, badge) plus bootstrap-rtl.min.css for RTL rendering. Custom wrappers like custom-style.css and amsify.select.css layer on top; changing the AdminLTE major version would silently break every admin page's markup.

nodes.label: Shopfront Theme Asset Contract
nodes.rationale: The customer-facing shell is a separate asset tree (/assets/shop/css/vendor/bootstrap.min.css + /assets/shop/css/main.css) with html lang=fa dir=rtl, deliberately independent of the AdminLTE admin tree (/assets/dist/...). It is the second of two parallel UI stacks maintained in the same project.

nodes.label: Static Asset URL Contract (/assets)
nodes.rationale: Templates hardcode absolute '/assets/...' URLs, so the directory layout under public/assets is a frozen contract between HTML and the static file mount. Asset paths are not parameterized or templated, so re-vendoring an asset requires editing head.html / footer.html by hand.

nodes.label: Admin Page View-Model Key Contract (.TITLE/.MESSAGE/.ERRORS/.OLDS/.AUTH)
nodes.rationale: Every admin page reads the same flat top-level keys — TITLE (page heading), MESSAGE (flash feedback), ERRORS.<field> (per-field validation), OLDS.<field> (form repopulation), AUTH (session identity) — from a single map passed as '.'. This is a map[string]any view model, so there is no compile-time type checking: a handler returning the wrong key produces an empty render, not an error.

nodes.label: .Data Pagination Envelope
nodes.rationale: List endpoints wrap results in a generic {Data: [...]} envelope, and pages consistently reach through two levels: .PRODUCTS.Data, .ATTRIBUTES.Data, .ATTRIBUTE.AttributeValues.Data, .Data.OrderItems.Data. The same envelope is reused for paginated collections and for single-order payloads, which is why admin_show_order mixes .Data.ID (scalar) with .Data.OrderItems.Data (list).

nodes.label: Admin Authentication (mobile + password, POST /admins/login)
nodes.rationale: Admin authentication is mobile-number plus password posted to /admins/login; the password field is rendered as type="text" and both fields are table-laid-out, and the page deliberately does NOT include head/navbar/sidebar/footer (its {{template "head"}} calls are commented out), so it renders unstyled inside whatever shell invokes it. Session identity then surfaces as .AUTH.FirstName in sidebar.html and admin_show_attribute.html.

nodes.label: Admin Order Status Transition (states 0-11)
nodes.rationale: The order status state machine (0 paying, 1 paid, 2 cancelled, 3 preparing, 4 ready-to-ship, 5 shipped, 6 in-transit, 7 delivered, 8 returned, 9 completed, 10 dispute, 11 unknown) is duplicated verbatim in the template's <select>, driven by the numeric Data.OrderStatus and accompanied by Data.OrderStatusText. The enum is therefore owned by the HTML as well as the Go domain, so adding a state requires a coordinated template change or the new state is unreachable from the admin UI.

nodes.label: Order Item Attribute Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Order lines render a nested range over .OrderItemAttributes.Data, meaning the order read model denormalizes the chosen attribute Title/Value pair onto each item so historical orders stay readable after a product's attributes change. The view depends on that snapshot rather than resolving attributes live from the catalog.

nodes.label: Upload Media Path Contract (/uploads/media/...)
nodes.rationale: Image fields are rendered as '/uploads/media/<folder>/<file>' where only the stored file name comes from the entity (.BRAND.Image, .CATEGORY.Image). Handlers must therefore return a bare relative filename, not a full URL or path — a full URL would produce '/uploads/media/brands//uploads/...'.

nodes.label: Admin AJAX Attribute Cascade (GET /admins/get-attributes/:id)
nodes.rationale: The attribute-value editor embeds an inline jQuery handler on #parent-category that fetches /admins/get-attributes/{parentId} and repopulates the #attribute select from response.Data. The handler is bound to an element (#parent-category) that this page never renders, and the attribute select is simultaneously server-rendered from .ATTRIBUTES.Data — so the AJAX branch is dead code copied from a category page, and the page is not self-contained: it depends on both a server-rendered list and an unrelated route.

nodes.label: Attribute / AttributeValue Administration
nodes.rationale: Attributes own a list of values: the values index reaches through the parent attribute (.ATTRIBUTE.AttributeValues.Data) and each value is edited against its parent via attribute_id plus a free-text value. The admin read model exposes the parent-attribute route (/admins/attributes/{id}) as the editing context for its values, so the parent is always the anchor of the value lifecycle.

nodes.label: Product Aggregate Data Surface (features, inventory, gallery, attributes)
nodes.rationale: The product admin view is a hub: it links out to five sub-resources (add-feature, show-gallery, add-attributes, add-inventory, edit) and renders .PRODUCT.Features.Data plus .PRODUCT.ProductInventories.Data in one page. The 'other operations' action bar linking to those same five routes is copy-pasted verbatim into admin_show_product_feature.html, so any route rename must be applied in both files.
nodes.norm_label: product aggregate data surface (features, inventory, gallery, attributes)

nodes.label: Read-only Form Pattern (DISABLED inputs in a formless table)
nodes.rationale: Read-only show pages are built as a <form> with no action containing only DISABLED inputs, so a brand looks editable but submits nothing; this reuses show-form CSS at the cost of implying editability. admin_show_brand.html omits the edit route entirely while admin_show_category.html links to /admins/categories/{id}/edit, showing the show pages are not uniform.
nodes.norm_label: read-only form pattern (disabled inputs in a formless table)

nodes.label: HTTP Error Page Templates
nodes.rationale:
The two error pages are registered inconsistently: 500.html wraps its markup in {{define "templates/html/errors/500"}} while 404.html is bare

404

with no define block. 404 therefore cannot be resolved by template name and must be loaded by Gin filename convention (no extension / errors/404), so any rename or loader change can break error rendering silently.

nodes.label: Customer Account Navigation Panel
nodes.rationale: The account sidebar renders identity with an explicit fallback (AUTH.FirstName + LastName, or AUTH.Mobile when no first name exists) and links out to /logout and /profile/edit while the remaining menu entries are inert '#' placeholders. It is the customer-side analogue of the admin sidebar, but it is session-scoped per-customer rather than a permission-based admin menu.

nodes.label: Mobile Bottom Navigation / Footer (footer_tmpl)
nodes.rationale: footer_tmpl is the shopfront closing block: a fixed d-lg-none mobile bottom bar (home, account, cart, orders, cart offcanvas via data-bs-toggle), a full footer with service icons, widget menus, newsletter form and trust seals, plus a scroll-progress 'go to top' widget. It uses Bootstrap 5 offcanvas data attributes, unlike the Bootstrap 4 + AdminLTE admin stack, so the two shells are on different Bootstrap majors.

nodes.label: Admin Route Navigation Contract (sidebar + navbar links)
nodes.rationale: The admin sidebar and navbar hardcode the full /admins/* route surface as literal hrefs (home, monitoring, banners, brands, categories, attributes, attribute-values, products, customers, orders). There is no route registry or reverse-lookup, so renaming a Gin route or prefix breaks navigation across every admin page that composes this partial, and menu entries for unimplemented screens (banner list, customers) are still rendered.
nodes.norm_label: admin route navigation contract (sidebar + navbar links)

nodes.label: Template Debug Context Dump
nodes.rationale: Three admin pages contain leftover debugging: a {{range $a,$key:=.}} dump of the whole view model (admin_show_attribute.html, admin_login.html) plus a stray 'ss' literal and a .AUTH.FirstName probe. Because the view model is map[string]any, this is the only in-template way to inspect it, and it leaks session fields into the rendered admin page.

nodes.label: Passwordless Mobile-Only Login
nodes.rationale: The login form POSTs to /login with a single field (name=mobile, type=number) and a 'remember me' checkbox; there is no password field anywhere. Authentication is therefore a passwordless OTP flow keyed on the Iranian mobile number: the login step only harvests the number and the following step verifies a code.

nodes.label: Address Form Repopulation (.OLDS / .ERRORS / .AUTH.Address)
nodes.rationale: Every shipping field uses the same three-way fallback: re-render the just-submitted value from .OLDS (a slice, hence `range`), else fall back to the customer's saved .AUTH.Address fields, else leave empty; .ERRORS drives both border-danger classes and per-field Persian messages. This keeps a failed POST from discarding the shopper's typed address while still prefilling from the stored default.

nodes.label: Standalone Checkout Shell (bypasses site layout)
nodes.rationale: Both order-result pages and the shipping step deliberately skip header_tmpl/mobile_side_menu_tmpl and ship their own inline `header-shopping` block plus a `mini-footer`, so post-checkout pages carry no cart badge, no live search and no navigation coupling to the session-scoped header that requires .AUTH.

nodes.label: Unwired Static Home Markup
nodes.rationale: The home page is still mostly hardcoded theme demo content: product names/prices are literals, no product rows are ranged over a data field (only {{.TITLE}} is bound), and product links point at the static assets' own filenames (`search.html`, `single-product.html`, `single-product-not-available.html`) rather than the real `/product/:sku/:slug` and `/search/:slug` routes. The only live binding is the composed partial shell.
